title: HAMNO: A Hierarchical Adaptive Multi-scale Neural Operator with Physics-Informed Learning for Dynamical Systems
title_zh: HAMNO：用于动力系统的层次自适应多尺度神经算子与物理信息学习
abstract_en: Neural operators provide a powerful framework for learning solution mappings of partial differential equations directly in function space. However, many existing architectures still struggle to represent nonlinear time-dependent systems that involve multi-scale structures, long-range interactions, and stable long-time evolution. In this work, we introduce the Hierarchical Adaptive Multi-scale Neural Operator (HAMNO), a neural-operator architecture that combines local convolutional representations, global spectral operators, and hierarchical encoder-decoder processing. The central component of HAMNO is a data-dependent gating mechanism that adaptively balances local and global information at each spatial location, allowing the model to resolve fine-scale features while preserving long-range dependencies. We further develop a physics-informed extension, PI-HAMNO, based on a multi-objective loss strategy that combines data fitting with strong- and weak-form physics constraints. The strong-form term penalizes the domain-integrated squared PDE residual in physical coordinates, while the weak-form term is constructed by multiplying the governing residual by finite-element test functions and evaluating the resulting element integrals using centroid-based tetrahedral quadrature. The framework is evaluated on non-periodic Allen-Cahn (AC), Cahn-Hilliard (CH), and Swift-Hohenberg (SH) equations defined on cubic domains. Across long-horizon rollout, data-limited training, out-of-distribution initial-condition shifts, and random-seed variations, HAMNO improves predictive accuracy over standard neural-operator baselines, while PI-HAMNO further enhances stability, physical consistency, and data efficiency. The implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/MBamdad/HAMNO .
abstract_zh: 本文提出 Hierarchical Adaptive Multi-scale Neural Operator（HAMNO），用于学习偏微分方程（PDE）动力系统的解映射。针对现有神经算子在非线性时变系统中难以同时建模多尺度结构、长程相互作用和长时间稳定演化的问题，HAMNO 结合局部卷积表示、全局谱算子与层次化 encoder-decoder 处理。其核心是数据依赖的门控机制，可在每个空间位置自适应平衡局部与全局信息，从而兼顾细尺度特征解析和长程依赖保持。作者进一步提出物理信息扩展 PI-HAMNO，通过多目标损失联合数据拟合、强形式物理约束与弱形式物理约束：强形式项惩罚物理坐标中的区域积分 PDE 残差平方，弱形式项将控制方程残差与有限元测试函数相乘，并用基于质心的四面体求积计算单元积分。实验在立方域上的非周期 Allen-Cahn（AC）、Cahn-Hilliard（CH）和 Swift-Hohenberg（SH）方程上进行。结果显示，在长时域 rollout、低数据训练、分布外初始条件偏移和随机种子变化等设置下，HAMNO 相比标准神经算子基线具有更高预测精度；PI-HAMNO 进一步提升了稳定性、物理一致性和数据效率。
key_points_zh: 提出 HAMNO，将局部 convolutional representation、global spectral operator 与层次 encoder-decoder 结合，以提升多尺度动力系统建模能力。
核心数据依赖 gating mechanism 在每个空间位置自适应融合局部细节与全局长程信息，缓解长时间演化中的误差累积和稳定性问题。
提出 PI-HAMNO，通过同时加入 strong-form PDE residual 与 weak-form finite-element constraint，实现物理信息约束训练。
弱形式约束使用有限元 test functions，并通过 centroid-based tetrahedral quadrature 近似单元积分，适用于三维立方域 PDE。
在非周期 AC、CH、SH 方程上，HAMNO/PI-HAMNO 在长时预测、少数据、OOD 初始条件和随机种子鲁棒性方面优于常见 neural-operator baselines。

llm_assessment.comment: A neural-operator modeling contribution for physical systems, but it is outside the agent harness and self-improving platform scope.
llm_assessment.comment_zh: 该论文主要贡献在物理系统神经算子建模，基本不属于智能体运行框架或自改进平台范畴。
